label: PRECISION BUDGET
note: This ledger started empty. Every fact below was measured by this skill's own instrument, read out of the backlog, and promoted on purpose; nothing here was copied from a plan, a paper or a sibling skill. The digit budget is a claim that can fail, so its sufficiency is measured rather than assumed, and the starved figure is deliberately not pinned because it is noise.

facts.claim: the scan over n <= 200 fits inside the working precision the budget formula asks for
the scan over n <= 400 fits inside the working precision the budget formula asks for
the formula's digit count is not minimal; the budget carries slack digits beyond the last precision that still breaks the bound, so the formula is a safe over-estimate rather than a tight requirement
Pisot's bound is violated at every probed working precision below the crossover and holds at every one above it, so the crossover is the highest precision that still fails
Pisot's constant 2 is not a safe margin; the arithmetic attains it to within a few parts in 100 million, so the bound is essentially tight rather than slack
the knife edge is not a curiosity of phi; no algebraic base expands 1 the same way at every working precision, so every base flips somewhere in the sweep
the greedy expansion of 1 in base phi terminates at some working precisions and not at others, so the terminating set is a strict subset of the sweep
the modulus of the conjugate pair equals sqrt(1/lambda) exactly, so the two routes can never disagree
the digits of the maximum measured on a starved budget are not stable enough to pin as a ledger fact, because the working precision has to be right and not merely roughly right
